details.description: GPT-6 Luna is OpenAI's fast, cost-efficient model in the GPT-6 family, released September 22, 2026 alongside GPT-6 Sol as the successor to GPT-5.6 Luna. AWS's Bedrock blog describes it as built for high-frequency, repeatable tasks such as extracting information from large document collections, summarizing incoming material, classifying inputs and answering focused questions. It takes text and image input and produces text output, with a knowledge cutoff of May 18, 2026 and reasoning effort adjustable per request from none up to max.
advantages: Scores 37 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at max reasoning effort, well above the comparable-model median of 13.
AWS's Bedrock blog reports improved factual reliability and clearer result communication compared to its predecessor, GPT-5.6 Luna.
Supports reasoning effort adjustable per request, from none to max, to balance quality and responsiveness for each task.
Supports function calling, structured outputs, file search, web search, code interpreter, hosted shell, computer use and MCP tool use via the Responses API.
disadvantages: Output is text-only; the model does not generate images, audio or video.
Not compatible with Live sessions, Realtime, Assistants, fine-tuning, embeddings, or audio/video features.
Artificial Analysis measured a time-to-first-token of about 109 seconds at max reasoning effort, well above the roughly 2-second median for comparable reasoning models.
AWS positions Luna below GPT-6 Sol in capability, intended for high-volume, repeatable tasks rather than the complex, multistep reasoning work Sol handles.
use_cases: Extracting information from large document collections
